items.prompt: Describe how to prepare a burette and pipette before a titration.
items.canonical_answer: Rinse the pipette with the solution it will deliver and the burette with the solution it will contain. Fill the burette, remove the air bubble from its jet and read the meniscus at eye level.
marking_guidance: Sequence: rinse, fill and remove the jet bubble. Reagent or apparatus: name the pipette and burette solutions. Condition: read at eye level. Observation or result: no air remains in the jet.
items.provenance: Authored for the 8224 thin Paper 3 structural exemplar from Annexe A.

items.prompt: Accurate titres are 24.35 cm³, 24.40 cm³ and 24.70 cm³. Calculate the mean concordant titre.
items.canonical_answer: The concordant pair is 24.35 and 24.40 cm³ because they differ by 0.05 cm³. Mean = (24.35 + 24.40) ÷ 2 = 24.375 cm³, so 24.38 cm³.
marking_guidance: Relationship or equation: mean of concordant values. Conversion and substitution: use 24.35 and 24.40 only. Answer, unit and significant figures: 24.38 cm³.
items.provenance: Authored for the 8224 thin Paper 3 structural exemplar from Annexe A.

items.prompt: A learner measures the 25.0 cm³ aliquot with a measuring cylinder. Suggest one realistic improvement and explain it.
items.canonical_answer: Use a 25.0 cm³ volumetric pipette. Criterion: volume uncertainty. Evidence: a pipette is calibrated to deliver the fixed aliquot more precisely than a measuring cylinder. Limitation addressed: uncertainty in the aliquot. Judgement: the concentration calculated from it is more reliable.
marking_guidance: Criterion: volume uncertainty. Evidence: pipette calibration. Limitation: measuring-cylinder precision. Judgement: improved reliability.

items.prompt:
A learner pipettes 25.00 cm³ of solution X into a flask and titrates it with 0.1000 mol dm⁻³ solution Y. X and Y react in a 1:1 mole ratio.

| run | initial burette reading / cm³ | final burette reading / cm³ |
|---|---:|---:|
| rough | 0.10 | 24.80 |
| 1 | 1.20 | 25.55 |
| 2 | 0.35 | 24.75 |
| 3 | 2.10 | 26.80 |

(a) Record the titre for each run in a new results column. [3]
(b) Identify the concordant titres and calculate their mean. [3]
(c) Calculate the concentration of X. [6]
(d) Explain why the rough titre is not included in the mean. [2]
(e) Identify one significant source of uncertainty in judging the endpoint and suggest a realistic improvement. [4]
(f) State two features of a correctly formatted titration table. [2]
items.canonical_answer:
(a) Rough 24.70 cm³; run 1 24.35 cm³; run 2 24.40 cm³; run 3 24.70 cm³.
(b) Runs 1 and 2 are concordant; mean = (24.35 + 24.40) ÷ 2 = 24.38 cm³.
(c) 24.375 cm³ = 0.024375 dm³. n(Y) = 0.1000 × 0.024375 = 0.0024375 mol. The ratio is 1:1, so n(X) = 0.0024375 mol. 25.00 cm³ = 0.02500 dm³. c(X) = 0.0024375 ÷ 0.02500 = 0.09750 mol dm⁻³.
(d) The rough run locates the endpoint and is not an accurate repeat.
(e) The colour change is judged by eye and may be overshot. Add titrant dropwise near the endpoint over a white tile while swirling, so the first permanent colour change is detected with less excess titrant.
(f) Headings give quantity and unit, and all burette readings use consistent decimal places.
marking_guidance: Apparatus and method: pipette, burette and endpoint procedure. Observations or data table: titres with quantity/unit headings. Working: conversion, cV and 1:1 ratio. Conclusion: 0.09750 mol dm⁻³. Error: subjective endpoint. Improvement: dropwise addition over a white tile.
